solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Want to contain creeper that's prickly

indicators.note: to contain asks the first word's synonym to hold the next one inside it

parts.note: to want something is to wish for it
an asp is a snake, something that creeps along the ground

explanation.surface: Someone longs to grow a thorny climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeper' suggests a climbing plant, but here it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish describes someone irritable and quick to sting, a synonym for prickly in temper.

clue.text: Disgruntled pig Dawn found in dry valley

indicators.note: disgruntled suggests upset, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An unhappy pig belonging to someone named Dawn turns up in an arid valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A wind gap is a geography term for a dry notch in a ridge once cut by a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind gap is a pass through a ridge with no stream flowing through it, a dry valley.

parts.note: broadcasting suggests radio, but it also means scattering seed widely by hand in a field

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scatters seed by hand in a field is literally broadcasting outdoors.

clue.text: Sit in a loo perhaps hopefully in this

definitions.text: Sit in a loo perhaps hopefully in this

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A person sitting in the toilet hopes to be left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers SIT IN A LOO; the whole clue also describes the state of solitude a loo-sitter hopes for.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is being apart from others, the privacy one hopes for in a locked cubicle.

clue.text: Walked a long way for some gnocchi, kedgeree etc.

indicators.note: for some tells us to take just a portion of the letters running across these words

explanation.surface: Someone trekked far to get Italian dumplings and a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: KEDGEREE is a British breakfast dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike is to take a long walk, so hiked means walked a long way.

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark is a Spanish army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior military officer, so this is a straightforward example.

clue.text: Lasting a long time with the continental record

parts.note: chronic describes something that persists over a long period
le is French for the, a continental word

explanation.surface: A long-standing European archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the continental' means 'the' in a European language, here French LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical record of events in order.

indicators.note: missing means the pass word is dropped from the fall word

parts.note: to collapse is to fall down
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and tumbles, failing to make a pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor error.

clue.text: Put almost all letters of 'gloominess' in different order to produce new word

indicators.note: in different order spells out that the remaining letters are rearranged
almost all letters of says to take the word bar its final letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange most of the letters of a gloomy word into something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all letters of' drops the last S of GLOOMINESS; 'in different order' shuffles the rest. 'Put' and 'to produce' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined term, which is exactly a new word.

parts.note: to watch is to look
to watch is also to see

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a pair of wristwatches for a quick check.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is informal for a quick glance or inspection.

parts.note: fresh means new
a yorker is a cricket delivery pitched right at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: A new parcel arrives for someone living in town.
explanation.walkthrough: A YORKER is a ball in cricket bowled to land at the batsman's feet; 'delivery' is the cricket word for a bowled ball, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the largest American metropolis is called by this demonym, an example of a city dweller.

clue.text: Sweltering, floating in river, leading to exposure

indicators.note: floating in places the hot word within the river's name, like something drifting in water

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
sweltering means very hot

explanation.surface: On a hot day someone drifts down a river and gets sunburnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposure' looks like sunburn after the swim, but it is a single frame of film.
explanation.definitionFit: In photography an exposure is one picture taken on film, hence a snapshot.

clue.text: Shelter in sound by a European lake

indicators.note: in sound tells us the shelter word is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: to shelter someone is to guard them

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover in a noisy spot beside a lake on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be a stretch of water, which suits the lake surface, but it means said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Garda in northern Italy is the largest lake in that country, so it is one European lake.

clue.text: Risky rendition of a rude song

indicators.note: a rendition is a performance or version, so the letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: Singing a vulgar ditty might land the singer in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous carries risk, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Loyal Irishman in charge imprisons threesome

indicators.note: imprisons means the outer pieces lock the trio up inside them

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A faithful Irish officer locks up three people.
explanation.definitionFit: Being patriotic means being devoted to one's country, a kind of loyalty.

definitions.meaning: revolted means disgusted or put off
a driver who left the main road and went into a side road did this

explanation.surface: Disgusted, someone swerved into a minor lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disgusted means being put off something; the literal sense is leaving the main road.

parts.note: though means even if

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters of put are set down wrongly

explanation.surface: Something was made up even if it was expressed badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To concoct an idea is to invent or devise it, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Plant I have located behind church

indicators.note: located behind places the I-have contraction after the church abbreviation

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone has a plant growing at the back of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are a herb of the onion family, an example of a plant.

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
a grill is a grating of bars

explanation.surface: A chef discovers a fish on a grating.
explanation.definitionFit: To chargrill is to cook food over very high heat on a grill.

indicators.note: round means the go word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to travel around a single Continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in north-west Italy, an example of a European city.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight acquires a ferocious beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild animal' looks like one phrase, but 'wild' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat of the striped Asian kind is an example of an animal.

indicators.note: windy suggests letters blown about and scrambled into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A breezy seaside walkway is nevertheless friendly to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeting someone with arms wide open is a gesture of warm welcome.

parts.note: dry humour is sarcastic or ironic

indicators.note: said means the contraction is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: the contraction I'd, as spoken

explanation.surface: Someone recalls making a cutting remark without tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry-eyed means not weeping, so it is without crying.

clue.text: Would marksman who is rusty practise with it?

definitions.text: Would marksman who is rusty practise with it?

parts.words: Would marksman who is rusty practise with it?
parts.note: a shooter out of practice is rusty, but read literally a rusty mechanism needs lubricating with a tool that squirts lubricant

explanation.surface: A question about how an out-of-practice shooter should train.
explanation.definitionFit: This lubricating tool fires grease into machinery, a gun that would treat literal rust.

parts.note: the drops are beads of moisture on the skin produced by hard labour

explanation.definitionFit: Perspiration forms in drops when the body works hard.

indicators.note: shorter than means the usual word is cut short at its end

parts.note: normal means usual

explanation.surface: A woman is smaller than average.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's name, an example of a lady.

clue.text: Stout tummies before end of day

parts.note: guts are bellies or tummies

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Fat bellies come before the day is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' suggests fat, matching tummies, but it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean brave and resolute, which is what gutsy means.

indicators.note: leaving means the king's letter departs from the crowd word

parts.note: a throng is a crowd
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king strips off and leaves a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather.

clue.text: During day before's all right to call up

indicators.note: during puts the all-right word inside the day-before word

parts.note: eve is the day before a festival
OK means all right

explanation.surface: On the eve of something it's fine to summon someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', and 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or feeling is to summon or call it up.

indicators.note: tours means the name goes all the way around the other letters

parts.note: Terry is short for Terence

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of riot are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Terence goes round the scene of a destructive riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the four letters to ITOR before 'tours' wraps the name around them; 'Terence' looks like the anagram's fodder but gives its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory is a region or tract of land, a synonym for area.

parts.note: soft means quiet
a spinning top is a toy that turns

explanation.surface: A silent spinning toy changes into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like an adjective, but it is a car with a folding roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A car whose fabric roof folds down is a convertible, so the two terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Maintained supporter to have negotiated deal outside

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the supporter word
negotiated suggests the letters of deal are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: Someone claimed a backer had brokered a deal from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' makes ALED, which 'outside' wraps around the supporter; 'to have' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege something is to maintain or assert it without proof.
